title: The Big brown trunk
subtitle: 家庭生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）
meta: 主题语境：家庭生活（人与自我·生活与学习·个人、家庭、社区及学校生活）　|　核心词汇：big　|　正文 330 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 big 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1964 the keeper wrote of ① a big brown trunk in the register, and everybody in the zoo said at once that it was ② bigger than the one named there the year before. Three seasons on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the keeper, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the big ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the biggest brown trunk anybody in the zoo had ever seen, or so the register for March 1958 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too big to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the child who had come to help; the big ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the fence at the far shed, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a big decision for them all, and said that no child in his right mind would call it ⑥ as big as the decision for them all they had once had in the old zoo. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was big or not, and he said so.

By 1971 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the register. What the line asked for was ⑦ something big, and nothing besides. The child from the next zoo called the whole plan ⑧ quite big; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the register kept the names of the big ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1974, twice over, she wrote of another big brown trunk in the same register, and the work, which took two seasons, seemed ⑨ bigger than anybody had expected. ⑩ The biggest decision for them all in the whole zoo, she said in 1976, was the one she could never quite name; the big ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 大（前置定语 a big brown trunk：1964 年饲养员在饲养台账里记下的那件大的箱子）
B. adj. 大／重大（比较级 bigger than：文中两处，一处比棕色的大箱子，一处比预想）
C. adj. 大／重大（最高级 the biggest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 大（表语 too big to do：母亲觉得它太大，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 重大（前置定语 a big decision for them all：叔叔把整件事称作一桩重大的决定）
F. adj. 重大（同级比较 as big as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩关乎众人的决定相比）
G. adj. 重大（后置定语 something big：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 重大（受程度副词修饰 quite big：那位孩子的评价）

items.q: a big decision for them all
The biggest decision for them all in

answers.why: big 意为“大”，1964 年饲养员在饲养台账里记下的是“一件大的箱子”，此处作前置定语 a big brown trunk。
big 意为“大”，此处用比较级 bigger than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
big 意为“大”，饲养台账上 三月 那行字说它是兽舍里最大的一件，故用最高级 the biggest brown trunk。
big 意为“大”，母亲认为这件东西“太大了，谁也用不上”，too big to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
big 意为“重大”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩重大的决定”，此处作前置定语 a big decision for them all。
big 意为“重大”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩关乎众人的决定一样重大”，同级比较用 as big as。
big 意为“重大”，饲养台账上那半行字要的是“重大的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something big。
big 意为“重大”，邻兽舍来的那位孩子认为这套计划“相当重大”，quite 修饰原级 big。
big 意为“重大”，1974 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要重大”，故用比较级 bigger than。
big 意为“重大”，母亲 1976 年说的是“整个兽舍里最重大的那一桩”，故用最高级 the biggest decision for them all。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1964 年，饲养员在饲养台账里记下了一件大的箱子。（a big brown trunk）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更大。（bigger than …）
母亲觉得它太大，谁也用不上。（too big to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩重大的决定。（a big decision for them all）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩关乎众人的决定一样重大。（as big as …）
到了 1971 年，饲养台账上只剩半行字：要的是一件重大的东西。（something big）
answers: In 1964 the keeper wrote of a big brown trunk in the register.
Everybody said it was bigger than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too big to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a big decision for them all.
He said nobody would call it as big as the decision for them all they had once had.
By 1971 the register asked for nothing but something big.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 big 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1964 the keeper wrote of a big brown trunk in the register, and nobody forgot it.
It was the biggest brown trunk in the zoo, or so the register says.
My mother thought it too big to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a big decision for them all, and nobody argued with him.
The child from the next zoo called the plan quite big, and everybody laughed.
The big ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
